name: The Sahara
scope: The world's largest hot desert, spanning North Africa. T1: the Sahara is about the size of the United States or China (~9.2 million km sq) — the biggest hot desert on Earth. T2: as recently as ~6,000 years ago it was a GREEN savanna of lakes, rivers, hippos and giraffes (the African Humid Period); rock paintings at Tassili n'Ajjer show cattle herders and swimmers where only sand is now. T3: a 40-km bullseye visible from orbit — the 'Eye of the Sahara' (Richat Structure) near Ouadane, Mauritania — is NOT an impact crater but an eroded dome of rock layers (invert the wonder: the from-space bullseye is the hook, 'eroded rock dome' the answer). T4: dust lifted from the Bodele Depression in Chad blows across the Atlantic and fertilizes the AMAZON, delivering roughly 22,000 tons of phosphorus a year — the desert feeds the rainforest. T5: the Sahara isn't mostly dunes — sand seas (ergs) cover only ~25%; the rest is rocky hamada plateaus, gravel reg, and the volcanic Tibesti Mountains, whose Emi Koussi is the Sahara's highest peak (~3,415 m). Extra rungs (deep): radar has found a buried ancient river system (the Tamanrasset paleoriver) beneath the sand; the Ounianga lakes of Chad survive in hyperarid desert on underground water (UNESCO); the great dunes of Erg Chebbi in Morocco; the green-to-desert flip happened in only ~1-2 centuries.
source: Grokipedia (checked first) + Wikipedia 'Sahara' and 'Richat Structure'; NASA Earth Observatory (Richat Structure; Saharan dust fertilizing the Amazon); Nature Scitable 'Green Sahara: African Humid Periods'. Verified: green Sahara ~6,000 yr BP with Tassili rock art; Richat = ~40 km eroded magmatic dome, not an impact crater; Bodele dust delivers ~22,000 t/yr phosphorus to the Amazon.
framing_note: Wonder-tour voice, scene-led — never 'what is the largest desert?'. Key accuracy rail: the Eye of the Sahara is an eroded geologic DOME, explicitly NOT a meteor crater or a 'lost Atlantis' — distractors are that pseudoscience plus real features. Green-Sahara timing (~6,000 yr) is solid; frame the abruptness as recent research. Dinner-test payoff: Saharan dust fertilizing the Amazon (T4). Lane: the Tassili rock art and cattle-herding are this PLACE's ancient marvel (geography), not a history-bank episode; hippos/giraffes are scenery — keep answers as place-facts, never animal biology.

name: The Atacama
scope: A hyperarid desert down Chile's northern coast. T1: the Atacama is the driest nonpolar place on Earth — some weather stations have NEVER recorded a drop of rain, and parts may go decades between showers. T2: its skies are the clearest and driest anywhere, so the world's great telescopes live here — ALMA on the Chajnantor plateau and the Very Large Telescope on Cerro Paranal (invert: the no-rain/clear-sky superlative is the hook, 'the world's observatories' the answer). T3: NASA tests Mars rovers here because the sterile, bone-dry soil is Earth's closest match to the surface of Mars (a 'Mars analog'). T4: once every few years a freak rain wakes long-dormant seeds and the sand erupts into the 'desierto florido' — the flowering desert — a carpet of millions of blooms. T5: the Chinchorro people mummified their dead on this coast ~7,000 years ago — the world's OLDEST artificial mummies, made ~2,000 years before Egypt's. Extra rungs (deep): the 86-m Atacama Giant geoglyph on Cerro Unita (purpose debated); the salt pillars of Valle de la Luna; the nitrate 'white gold' ghost town of Humberstone (UNESCO); the lithium-rich brine of the Salar de Atacama.
source: Grokipedia (checked first) + Wikipedia 'Atacama Desert' and 'Chinchorro mummies'; ESO / NASA on Atacama observatories and Mars-analog research; National Geographic and Ancient Origins on Chinchorro. Verified: driest nonpolar desert with stations lacking recorded rain; ALMA/VLT sites; Chinchorro artificial mummification from ~5050 BC, ~2,000 yr before Egypt.
framing_note: Scene-led wonder tour. Accuracy rail: state 'driest' carefully — some STATIONS have no recorded rain, but coastal fog (camanchaca) still brings moisture, so frame as 'driest nonpolar desert', not 'no water ever'. The Atacama Giant's meaning is DISPUTED (astronomical calendar?) — label it. Dinner-test payoff: the Chinchorro mummies (T5), oldest on Earth, a cultural creation genuinely born in this desert (geography's lane: the place + its people's marvel, not a history-bank episode). Distractors: other real driest/clearest-sky places and other ancient mummy cultures keep all four live.

name: The Namib
scope: A fog desert on Namibia's Atlantic coast. T1: the Namib is among the OLDEST deserts on Earth — arid for at least 55 million years. T2: at Sossusvlei, star-shaped dunes tower 300+ m; 'Big Daddy' reaches ~325 m, among the tallest dunes anywhere. T3: at Deadvlei, a blinding-white clay pan cradles the black skeletons of camelthorn trees that died ~900 years ago and are simply too dry to rot — scorched by sun, NOT petrified into stone (accuracy rail). T4: the Skeleton Coast is a graveyard of shipwrecks and whale bones, where cold fog and the Benguela current wreck ships and the great dunes run straight into the Atlantic surf. T5: the desert's grasslands are pocked with 'fairy circles' — bare rings meters wide — whose cause is genuinely DEBATED between termite engineering and plants competing for scarce water (label DISPUTED). Extra rungs (deep): fog is the only reliable water and the whole ecosystem 'drinks' it; the Welwitschia plant can live 1,000-2,000 years; diamonds and the sand-buried ghost town of Kolmanskop; 'Namib' means 'vast place' in Nama.
source: Grokipedia (checked first) + Wikipedia 'Namib', 'Sossusvlei', 'Deadvlei', 'Skeleton Coast'; info-namibia and Wilderness on dune heights; peer-reviewed fairy-circle debate (Getzin termite vs. plant-competition hypotheses). Verified: Namib arid 55+ Myr; Big Daddy ~325 m; Deadvlei camelthorns ~900 yr and desiccated (not petrified).
framing_note: Wonder-tour voice, scene first. Accuracy rail: the Deadvlei trees are DESICCATED (dried, ~900 yr), not fossilized/petrified — a classic wrong distractor to keep live. Fairy circles = OPEN QUESTION: present two competing real hypotheses, no verdict. Dinner-test payoff: Deadvlei's 900-year-old black dead trees (T3). Lane: the Welwitschia is a PLANT landscape emblem (fine for geography); do NOT drift into the fog-basking beetle's anatomy (animal bank) — keep any fog rung as the PLACE-process (a desert watered by ocean fog).

name: The Gobi
scope: A cold rain-shadow desert across Mongolia and northern China. T1: the Gobi is a COLD desert — a place where summer can hit +45 C yet winter plunges to -40 C, colder than most of Canada. T2: it exists because it sits in the RAIN SHADOW of the Himalayas and Tibetan Plateau — the mountains wring the monsoon dry before it can reach the basin (teach 'rain shadow'). T3: at the red-sandstone Flaming Cliffs (Bayanzag), Roy Chapman Andrews's 1923 expedition found the world's first recognized dinosaur EGGS — the discovery that proved dinosaurs laid eggs. T4: the Khongoryn Els or 'Singing Dunes' boom a deep drone as sand avalanches down slopes ~300 m tall. T5: the Gobi is the last wild refuge of the two-humped Bactrian camel — fewer than ~1,000 truly wild ones remain (place-fact: the desert is its last stronghold). Extra rung: the Gobi is slowly GROWING toward Beijing, driving China's tree-planting 'Great Green Wall'.
source: Grokipedia 'Flaming Cliffs' (checked first) + Wikipedia 'Gobi Desert' and 'Flaming Cliffs'; AMNH on Roy Chapman Andrews and the 1923 dinosaur-egg discovery. Verified: cold-desert temperature swing; rain-shadow origin; 1923 first recognized dinosaur eggs at Bayanzag; wild Bactrian camel last refuge.
framing_note: Scene-led. Accuracy rail: teach 'rain shadow' before testing it; the dinosaur-egg find is 1923 at the Flaming Cliffs (Roy Chapman Andrews, a real paleontologist — not a movie hero). Dinner-test payoff: the first dinosaur eggs ever found (T3). Lane border: the Bactrian-camel rung's ANSWER stays a PLACE-fact (the Gobi is its last wild home), NOT the camel's hump biology (that's the animal bank). Distractors: other cold deserts and other famous fossil sites keep choices live.

name: Death Valley
scope: A below-sea-level furnace in California's Mojave. T1: Furnace Creek recorded 56.7 C (134 F) on July 10, 1913 — the hottest reliable AIR temperature ever measured on Earth (some experts dispute the exact reading; note it). T2: Badwater Basin is the lowest point in North America, 86 m BELOW sea level — a bright salt flat cracked into hexagons. T3: on Racetrack Playa, heavy 'sailing stones' glide across the flat mud leaving long trails behind them; the mystery was SOLVED in 2014 — thin sheets of winter ice, floated by meltwater and nudged by light wind, drag the rocks. T4: Death Valley is a rain-shadow desert — five mountain ranges strip Pacific storms of their moisture before they ever reach the valley floor. T5: after a rare wet winter the dead-looking floor erupts in a 'superbloom' of wildflowers from seeds that waited years. Extra rung: the valley is still sinking as the crust pulls apart (Basin and Range extension).
source: Grokipedia (checked first) + Wikipedia 'Death Valley' and 'Highest temperature recorded on Earth'; NPS Death Valley weather pages; PNAS/Scripps 2014 sailing-stones study (Norris & Lorenz). Verified: 56.7 C air record July 10 1913 (disputed by some); Badwater -86 m; sailing stones solved 2014 (ice + wind).
framing_note: Scene-led; invert the superlative (the 134 F record is the hook). Accuracy rail: 1913 is the hottest reliably-recorded AIR temperature — keep it DISTINCT from the Lut Desert's satellite SURFACE-temperature record (a perfect adjacent distractor). The sailing-stones answer is the SOLVED mechanism (ice + wind), a settled 2014 finding — NOT 'still a mystery'. Dinner-test payoff: the self-moving sailing stones (T3).

name: Uluru and the Red Centre
scope: A giant red monolith in Australia's Red Centre. T1: Uluru rises 348 m straight out of the flat desert — a single vast rock (an 'inselberg') visible from far across the plain. T2: what shows above ground is only the tip — the arkose sandstone continues roughly 2.5 km DOWN underground, like an iceberg. T3: it blazes fiery red at sunrise and sunset because iron in the rock has literally RUSTED — the surface is oxidized iron (invert: the color-change wonder is the hook, 'rusted iron' the answer). T4: Uluru is sacred to its Aboriginal custodians, the Anangu, whose Tjukurpa ('Dreaming') law maps ancestral stories onto its caves and waterholes; climbing it was permanently banned in 2019 at their request. T5: 30 km west stand the 36 red domes of Kata Tjuta ('many heads'), whose tallest dome rises even higher than Uluru — ~546 m above the plain. Extra rung: the rock is ~550 million years old, tilted nearly vertical by ancient mountain-building.
source: Grokipedia 'Uluru' (checked first) + Wikipedia 'Uluru'; Parks Australia (uluru.gov.au) on Anangu, Tjukurpa, and the 2019 climbing ban; Britannica on geology. Verified: 348 m high, ~2.5 km underground extent, Mutitjulu arkose reddened by iron oxide; Anangu custodianship and 2019 climb closure; Kata Tjuta tallest dome ~546 m.
framing_note: Reverent wonder-tour voice. vision_mandated TRUE: the Anangu custodianship, Tjukurpa, and the 2019 climbing ban are living-culture matters — present them straight and respectfully, not as quaint legend or a 'debate'. Accuracy rail: the red color is oxidized (rusted) iron on grey arkose, and the 2.5-km underground extent is the payoff. Dinner-test payoff: Uluru is really an 'iceberg' ~2.5 km deep (T2). Lane: this is the PLACE and its custodians' meaning (geography), not a colonial-history episode.

name: The Taklamakan
scope: A shifting-sand basin in western China's Tarim Basin. T1: the Taklamakan's name warns 'go in and you don't come out' — nicknamed the 'Sea of Death,' it's ringed by some of the highest mountains on Earth (Tian Shan, Kunlun, Pamir). T2: its dunes shift so fast that entire Silk Road caravan cities (Loulan, Niya) were swallowed and BURIED under the sand. T3: the bone-dry sand naturally preserved the 'Tarim mummies' — ~4,000-year-old bodies with fair hair and finely woven wool cloth (their origins are genuinely DEBATED — label it). T4: the Tarim Basin is ENDORHEIC — rivers like the Tarim flow INTO the desert and simply vanish, never reaching any sea (teach 'endorheic'). T5: to cross it, China built a ~500-km desert highway and lined it with a drip-irrigated green shelterbelt to stop the marching dunes from burying the road.
source: Grokipedia (checked first) + Wikipedia 'Taklamakan Desert' and 'Tarim mummies'; Encyclopaedia Iranica on the Taklamakan. Verified: 'Sea of Death'/place-of-no-return name; buried Silk Road cities (Loulan, Niya); naturally-preserved Tarim mummies ~4,000 yr with woven textiles, ancestry debated; endorheic Tarim Basin; Tarim Desert Highway shelterbelt.
framing_note: Scene-led wonder tour. Accuracy rail: the Tarim mummies' ancestry is an OPEN research question — present the preservation and well-woven cloth as fact, the origins as debated, no verdict. Dinner-test payoff: Silk Road cities swallowed whole by moving dunes (T2). Lane/history_overlap: the Silk Road as a TRADE-ROUTE story belongs to history; here the geography angle is the DESERT burying the cities and mummifying the dead — keep answers place/landscape-facts.
history_overlap: Silk Road TRADE HISTORY (caravan routes, Marco Polo, cross-continental commerce) is a history-bank topic; this ladder stays on the desert's landscape (dunes burying cities, endorheic basin, natural mummification), so overlap is avoidable — flag only if a rung drifts into trade-route narrative.

name: The Rub' al Khali (Empty Quarter)
scope: The 'Empty Quarter' sand sea of southern Arabia. T1: the Rub' al Khali is the largest CONTINUOUS sand desert on Earth — an unbroken sand sea roughly the size of France (~650,000 km sq). T2: its dunes are among the tallest anywhere, rising up to ~250 m and marching in unbroken ridges dozens of km long. T3: beneath the sand lies Ghawar, the largest conventional oil field on Earth — the Empty Quarter sits atop an ocean of petroleum (invert: the barren emptiness above hides the world's richest oil below). T4: dry lakebeds show the Empty Quarter was dotted with freshwater LAKES just a few thousand years ago — a wetter 'Green Arabia.' T5: legend places 'Ubar'/Iram, the lost 'Atlantis of the Sands,' out here, said to be swallowed by the dunes — hunted for using satellite imagery (label LEGEND/DISPUTED).
source: Grokipedia (checked first) + Wikipedia "Rub' al Khali"; Guinness World Records 'largest continuous sand desert'; NASA Earth Observatory 'Ar Rub' al Khali Sand Sea'; Britannica. Verified: largest continuous sand desert (~650,000 km sq); dunes to ~250 m; Ghawar largest oil field beneath it; Holocene freshwater lakebeds; Ubar/Iram as legend searched via remote sensing.
framing_note: Scene-led. Accuracy rail: 'largest CONTINUOUS / sand desert' (the Sahara is larger overall but not continuous sand) — keep that precise; distractors are the Sahara and other ergs. Ubar is LEGEND: present the satellite search as real, the lost city as unproven. Dinner-test payoff: the world's biggest oil field hidden under the emptiest sand (T3). The Green-Arabia lake rung is solid paleoclimate.

name: The Lut Desert (Dasht-e Lut)
scope: Iran's Dasht-e Lut, the hottest ground on Earth. T1: satellites have clocked the Lut Desert's SURFACE at about 80.8 C (177 F) — the hottest ground temperature ever measured on the planet, hot enough to cook an egg on the sand. T2: it bakes that hot because black, lava-darkened sand soaks up sunlight and a ring of mountains traps the heat with almost no wind (the place-reason it's the hottest). T3: wind has carved the Lut into 'kaluts' — mile-long ridges (yardangs) that from above look like the streets of a ruined city (teach 'yardang'). T4: those landforms made the Lut Iran's first NATURAL UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016.
source: Grokipedia (checked first) + Wikipedia 'Dasht-e Lut'; NASA Science 'Iran's Lut Desert'; Science/AAAS on MODIS surface-temperature record; UNESCO World Heritage listing (2016). Verified: MODIS peak surface temp ~80.8 C (2018), up from 70.7 C (2005); dark heat-absorbing terrain; kaluts/yardangs; UNESCO 2016.
framing_note: Scene-led; invert the superlative. Accuracy rail: this is a SATELLITE SURFACE-temperature record — keep it DISTINCT from Death Valley's reliably-recorded AIR-temperature record (each is the perfect distractor for the other). Teach 'yardang/kalut' before testing. Dinner-test payoff: the 80.8 C fry-an-egg ground (T1).

name: The Sonoran Desert
scope: The green desert of Arizona and northwest Mexico. T1: the Sonoran is the ONLY place on Earth where the giant saguaro cactus grows wild — its silhouette exists naturally nowhere else. T2: a saguaro can live 150-200 years and top 12 m, yet it won't grow its first 'arm' until it's roughly 70 years old (invert: the giant arms are the hook, 'not until ~70 years old' the answer). T3: unlike almost every other desert, the Sonoran gets TWO rainy seasons — gentle Pacific winter rains and violent summer monsoons — which is why it's so lush and alive. T4: mild, nearly frost-free winters make it the most BIODIVERSE desert in North America, home to 2,000+ plant species (the place-reason it teems where other deserts stay bare). T5: at night the saguaro opens white flowers (Arizona's state flower); alongside grow the organ-pipe and the weird upside-down 'boojum' — a cactus forest found nowhere else.
source: Grokipedia (checked first) + Wikipedia 'Sonoran Desert' and 'Saguaro'; Saguaro National Park / Friends of Saguaro; Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum. Verified: saguaro endemic to Sonoran Desert; lifespan 150-200 yr, first arm ~50-75 yr; two rainy seasons (Pacific winter + summer monsoon); most biodiverse North American desert (2,000+ plant species).
framing_note: Scene-led wonder tour. Accuracy rail: 'only place the saguaro grows wild' is the anchor — distractors are other iconic cacti/deserts, never a 'a plant / a mineral' joke option. Dinner-test payoff: a saguaro grows no arms until ~70 years old (T2). Lane: the saguaro is a PLANT landscape-emblem — geography owns the desert's signature flora and WHY two rain seasons make it lush; do not stray into desert animals' biology (animal bank).

name: The Kalahari
scope: A red 'thirstland' across Botswana and Namibia. T1: the Kalahari's sand glows rusty RED from iron oxide — but it's a semi-desert 'thirstland,' not a true desert, catching just enough rain for grass and scattered trees. T2: the Okavango River pours INTO the Kalahari and dies there, fanning out into the Okavango Delta — a vast green wetland that never reaches any sea (teach 'endorheic' / inland delta). T3: the blinding Makgadikgadi salt pans are the ghost of a giant ancient lake — Lake Makgadikgadi — once bigger than Switzerland, which dried up thousands of years ago. T4: marooned on that white salt sea sits Kubu Island, a rocky ridge of ancient baobab trees that once stood on the vanished lake's shore. T5: the central Kalahari is the ancestral land of the San (Bushmen), among Earth's oldest continuous cultures, who find water in the driest sand through buried tsama melons and 'sip-wells' (knowledge born of this place).
source: Grokipedia (checked first) + Wikipedia 'Kalahari Desert', 'Okavango Delta', 'Lake Makgadikgadi', 'Makgadikgadi Pan'; UNESCO Okavango Delta listing. Verified: semi-arid 'thirstland'; Okavango endorheic inland delta; paleolake Makgadikgadi (80,000-275,000 km sq, dried by ~10,000 yr BP); Kubu Island baobabs on salt pan; San ancestral land.
framing_note: Scene-led. Accuracy rail: the Kalahari is technically a semi-arid 'thirstland' (it gets rain), a nuance worth keeping honest; the Okavango is a true endorheic inland delta. Dinner-test payoff: a mighty river that flows INTO the desert and simply dies (T2). Lane: the San rung honors living land-knowledge as a real cultural creation of this place — present respectfully, no romanticized 'noble savage' framing; it's a wonder-fact, not a contested-stance rung, so vision_mandated stays FALSE.

name: The 'Door to Hell' (Darvaza gas crater)
scope: A crater of fire in Turkmenistan's Karakum Desert. T1: in the middle of the Karakum sand sits the 'Door to Hell' (Darvaza) — a ~70-m-wide crater that has been ON FIRE continuously for over 50 years. T2: it wasn't natural — a Soviet gas-drilling rig collapsed into an underground cavern (commonly dated ~1971, though the date is disputed) and engineers set the escaping methane alight, expecting it to burn out in days; it never stopped. T3: Turkmenistan now wants to put it out or tap the gas, because the crater has leaked and burned methane for half a century.
source: Grokipedia 'Darvaza gas crater' (checked first) + Wikipedia 'Darvaza gas crater'; Popular Science and Discover Wildlife on recent extinguishing efforts. Verified: ~60-70 m wide, ~30 m deep; burning since ~1971 (date disputed, possibly 1980s); Soviet drilling collapse and deliberate ignition is the standard but not fully documented account; Turkmenistan seeking to reduce/extinguish it.
framing_note: A short 'strange place' gem, scene first. Accuracy rail: the exact ignition DATE is disputed (commonly 1971, possibly 1980s) and the 'lit deliberately to burn off gas' account is the standard but not fully documented story — hedge as such, no false precision. Dinner-test payoff: it's been burning nonstop for 50+ years (T1). Human-made, but a genuine famous desert landmark — geography's 'strange place' lane, no lane conflict.
